judged_text: The SalesforceCalendarService constructor now performs an unconditional token refresh against login.salesforce.com plus a credential DB write on every instantiation, with no check that the stored access token is still valid. Every booking, availability check, and cancellation for a Salesforce-connected user pays a round trip to Salesforce's OAuth endpoint and a DB write — previously the constructor did no network I/O and jsforce refreshed lazily only on demand — adding latency and rate-limit exposure to a hot path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new code refreshes the OAuth token via `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then immediately does `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no conditional check (e.g., access token expiry/validity) guarding this refresh/update, so every instantiation will incur a network round-trip and DB write. This is a concrete hot-path latency/rate-limit/architecture concern introduced by the diff, even if it may still be functionally correct.
